candidate_hypotheses.label: H1: Delay timing or repeat pattern is materially involved
candidate_hypotheses.mechanism: A brief send automation on selected words feeds an otherwise idle delay return, creating emphasis without continuous clutter.
candidate_hypotheses.evidence_needed: A current representative capture, exact phrase/tempo/scope, and matched-level comparison through the next musical event.
candidate_hypotheses.discriminating_test: Create a 100% wet delay aux, choose a value with available space, and automate the send only on one phrase-ending word.

candidate_hypotheses.label: H2: Feedback, filtering, or modulation is creating the problem
candidate_hypotheses.mechanism: Repeat generations may accumulate spectrum, noise, pitch movement, or density even when the first repeat timing is appropriate.
candidate_hypotheses.evidence_needed: Wet-only audition and repeat-by-repeat listening through the tail.
candidate_hypotheses.discriminating_test: Keep time fixed and change only feedback or feedback-loop color, then restore it.

candidate_hypotheses.label: H3: Stereo/phase/latency behavior is changing the dry source
candidate_hypotheses.mechanism: Short offsets, crossfeed, parallel routing, or compensation can create comb filtering, localization shifts, or mono cancellation.
candidate_hypotheses.evidence_needed: Mono check, polarity/correlation evidence, and path timing measurement where applicable.
candidate_hypotheses.discriminating_test: Center/narrow the delay or remove manual offsets, then compare before changing rhythm.

candidate_hypotheses.label: H4: The arrangement, performance, or automation does not leave a useful gap
candidate_hypotheses.mechanism: Repeats may collide with lyrics, hits, chord changes, and dense sections rather than being technically wrong.
candidate_hypotheses.evidence_needed: Phrase/section context, tempo map, and user report of where repeats collide.
candidate_hypotheses.discriminating_test: Automate one selected throw or mute the effect during dense events to test the arrangement explanation.

recommended_first_experiment.summary: Create a 100% wet delay aux, choose a value with available space, and automate the send only on one phrase-ending word.
recommended_first_experiment.action: Create a 100% wet delay aux, choose a value with available space, and automate the send only on one phrase-ending word.
recommended_first_experiment.why_this_first: It is designed to distinguish the leading explanation from level, routing, spectrum, stereo, performance, arrangement, and monitoring alternatives before adding more processing.

rationale: The immediate issue is that a brief send automation on selected words feeds an otherwise idle delay return, creating emphasis without continuous clutter. The first experiment changes one meaningful variable and produces causal information before a broader chain or preset is recommended.
logic_pro_steps: Loop the exact phrase or rhythmic passage where the delay should contribute, including the next important event or section boundary.
Save or note the current dry level, send/return level, delay time, feedback, filtering, stereo mode, and automation.
Create a 100% wet delay aux, choose a value with available space, and automate the send only on one phrase-ending word.
Change only one timing, feedback, filter, modulation, routing, or pan variable at a time.
Match perceived effect level before comparing groove, clarity, width, and repeat decay.
Replay the full mix, mono, and a second section before keeping the result.
starting_points: Begin with feedback at zero or very low and the wet contribution at zero, then add only enough to hear the first repeat in context.
Start from the nearest useful musical subdivision or a short single-repeat time, then nudge by ear around the groove.
Filter repeats so they support rather than duplicate the dry source; any frequency values are starting orientations, not presets.
Check the final repeat against the next lyric, hit, chord, or section boundary.
what_to_listen_for: Repeats should occupy deliberate rhythmic or spatial gaps rather than duplicate every important event.
The dry source should remain intelligible and correctly localized unless the artistic goal explicitly changes it.
Listen for clutter, harmonic clashes, comb filtering, feedback buildup, stereo-image movement, and mono cancellation.
Check whether the result survives a level-matched bypass and the next chord, lyric, hit, or section.
stop_rule: Stop or back off when the intended rhythm or space improves but repeats begin masking the source, crossing important events, destabilizing mono, or building uncontrollably.
stop_conditions: Stop or back off when the intended rhythm or space improves but repeats begin masking the source, crossing important events, destabilizing mono, or building uncontrollably.
undo_or_reset: Restore the saved send, return, delay time, feedback, filtering, stereo mode, automation, and routing, then replay the same passage.
undo: Restore the saved send, return, delay time, feedback, filtering, stereo mode, automation, and routing, then replay the same passage.
tradeoffs_and_risks: A louder repeat can appear better even when it disrupts groove or intelligibility.
Feedback, stereo offsets, modulation, and distortion can accumulate unexpectedly.
Repeats can cross chord changes, lyrics, and section boundaries and become arrangement conflicts.
A timing, performance, source, or monitoring problem may be mistaken for a delay-setting problem.
alternatives_if_wrong: Use short ambience or reverb when discrete repeats call too much attention to themselves.
Use real double tracking, arrangement gaps, note-length edits, or automation instead of delay.
Print and edit a special repeat pattern as an arrangement asset when live feedback is difficult to bound.
common_mistakes: Copying a decay, pre-delay, feedback, note value, filter, or wet percentage without matching the source and arrangement.
Judging the effect soloed or louder than bypass.
Changing timing, tone, level, feedback, stereo mode, and routing simultaneously.
Using ambience or repeats to solve a performance, arrangement, balance, editing, or source-selection problem.
do_not_assume: A common setting, tempo formula, room label, or forum answer is correct for this source and song.
A spectrum, waveform, model observation, or plug-in label proves the artistic complaint or its cause.
More width, length, density, feedback, brightness, or wet level is automatically better.
The first plausible cause is the true cause.
teaching_principle: Delay is arrangement in time: decide where each repeat belongs, how it changes, and when it must get out of the way.
